findings.problem: The new files `function_call_expr.go` and `tuple_cons_expr.go` (and their tests) do not use the `ast_` prefix. Every other AST node type in the package uses it, for example `ast_object_cons_expr.go` and `ast_expression.go`. The parse functions are also split inconsistently: `parseFunctionCallExpr` and `parseTupleConsExpr` live next to their types, but `parseObjectConsExpr` and `parseObjectConsKeyExpr` stay in `parser.go`.
findings.fix: Rename the files to `ast_function_call_expr.go`, `ast_function_call_expr_test.go`, `ast_tuple_cons_expr.go` and `ast_tuple_cons_expr_test.go`. Pick one place for parse functions. Either move `parseFunctionCallExpr` and `parseTupleConsExpr` into `parser.go` next to `parseObjectConsExpr`, or move `parseObjectConsExpr` and `parseObjectConsKeyExpr` into `ast_object_cons_expr.go`.

findings.problem: `parseTupleConsExpr` and `parseFunctionCallExpr` (`function_call_expr.go:59`) have the same body. Each loops over native sub-expressions, partitions the tokens, appends the tokens before each sub-expression, parses it with `parseExpression`, adds the node to a `nodeSet`, appends the leftover tokens and wraps the result in an `Expression`.
findings.fix: Extract a helper such as `parseSubExpressions(children *nodes, set nodeSet, natives []hclsyntax.Expression, from inputTokens)` that appends the parts and the trailing tokens. Each parser then becomes: create the node, call the helper, then `wrapExpr.wrap(...)`.

findings.problem: `FunctionCallExpr.args` (and `TupleConsExpr.elems` in `tuple_cons_expr.go:15`) is filled during parsing but nothing reads it. `Variables` walks `children` instead, and no accessor exposes it. The field is write-only state that has to be kept in sync for nothing.
findings.fix: Add public accessors that read the sets, matching `ObjectConsExpr.Items`: `func (call *FunctionCallExpr) Args() []*Expression` and `func (t *TupleConsExpr) Exprs() []*Expression`, each built from `nodeSet.List()`. If no accessors are wanted yet, remove the fields and the `Add` calls.

findings.problem: `AsObjectConsExpr`, `AsFunctionCallExpr`, `AsTupleConsExpr` and `asQuoted` are four copies of the same nil-check and type assertion on `e.wrapped.content`. This change added two of them. `AsObjectConsExpr` also has no doc comment, while the new methods do.
findings.fix: Add a generic helper, `func wrappedAs[T nodeContent](e *Expression) T { var zero T; if e.wrapped == nil { return zero }; t, _ := e.wrapped.content.(T); return t }`, and make each `As*` method a one-line call to it. Add a doc comment to `AsObjectConsExpr` that matches the other two.

findings.problem: `parseTemplateExpr` sets `expr.wrapped = expr.children.Append(quoted)` directly. It skips `Expression.wrap`, which every other wrapping parser now uses and which guards against wrapping twice.

`parseObjectConsExpr` reads `before.writerTokens`, `open.writerTokens` and `from.writerTokens` directly. The rest of the parser, including the new `parseFunctionCallExpr` and `parseTupleConsExpr`, uses the `inputTokens.Tokens()` accessor. It also uses `children` and `expr.children` for the same list in the same function.
findings.fix: Use `.Tokens()` everywhere in `parseObjectConsExpr`, and use the `children` local throughout (`node := children.Append(item)`).

findings.problem: `splitAtLineEnd` is a method on `*ObjectConsExpr` but never uses its receiver. It is a pure token helper, and it repeats the rule that a line comment ending in '\n' ends the line, which `partitionLineEndTokens` in `parser.go` already encodes.
findings.fix: Make it a package-level function, `splitAtLineEnd(toks Tokens) (Tokens, Tokens, bool)`, and update the three call sites. Put the shared check, whether a token ends a line (`TokenNewline`, or `TokenComment` whose bytes end in '\n'), in one small helper. Use that helper from both `splitAtLineEnd` and `partitionLineEndTokens`.

findings.problem: `appendItem` builds newline and comma `Token` literals inline, and `ObjectConsItem.init` builds the '=' token inline as well. They repeat the token construction that `NewExpressionAbsTraversal` and `generate.go` also do by hand.
findings.fix: Build them once with small helpers next to `newIdentToken` in `tokens.go`, for example `newNewlineToken()`, `newCommaToken()` and `newEqualToken(spacesBefore int)`, and use those helpers here.

findings.problem: `TestExpressionVariablesFunctionCallTupleCons` repeats the whole loop body of `TestExpressionVariablesObjectCons`. Two of its cases (`{ k = f(old.x) }` and `{ k = [old.x] }`) appear in both tables. Only the ObjectCons test also checks the count against hclsyntax.
findings.fix: Merge the two into one table-driven `TestExpressionVariables` with a single loop that keeps the hclsyntax variable-count check for every case, and remove the duplicate cases.

findings.problem: Every new test function repeats the same ParseConfig, `diags.HasErrors()`, `t.Fatalf` and `GetAttribute("a").Expr()` boilerplate. The same pattern appears in `ast_expression_test.go` and `function_call_expr_test.go`, even though the package already has a `mustParseConfig` helper in `ast_block_test.go`.
findings.fix: Add a test helper such as `mustParseAttrExpr(t, src) (*File, *Expression)` that calls `t.Helper()`, or reuse `mustParseConfig`, and use it in all the new tests.

kept.why: The two loops are the same except for the field names: partition, append before.Tokens(), parseExpression, AppendNode, set.Add, append the leftover tokens, then wrap. Function arguments and tuple elements are the same idea (an ordered list of sub-expressions), so one helper doesn't couple unrelated callers.

kept.why: grep shows FunctionCallExpr.args and TupleConsExpr.elems are only set up in the constructors and filled by Add. Nothing reads them: there is no accessor, and Variables walks children. They are write-only state.

kept.problem: `parseTemplateExpr` sets `expr.wrapped = expr.children.Append(quoted)` directly. It skips `Expression.wrap`, which every other wrapping parser now uses and which guards against wrapping twice.
kept.why: parseTemplateExpr repeats the body of Expression.wrap inline (expr.wrapped = expr.children.Append(quoted)) and skips the double-wrap guard. Every other wrapping parser calls wrap. The fix is one line and doesn't change behavior.

kept.problem: `parseObjectConsExpr` reads `before.writerTokens`, `open.writerTokens` and `from.writerTokens` directly. The rest of the parser, including the new `parseFunctionCallExpr` and `parseTupleConsExpr`, uses the `inputTokens.Tokens()` accessor. It also uses `children` and `expr.children` for the same list in the same function.
kept.fix: Use `.Tokens()` everywhere in `parseObjectConsExpr`, and use the `children` local throughout (`node := children.Append(item)`).
kept.why: In parseObjectConsExpr the same list is called both `children` and `expr.children` (`node := expr.children.Append(item)`). Tokens are read through `.writerTokens` while the rest of the parser uses `.Tokens()`. The same thing goes by two names in one function. The fix is cheap.

kept.problem: `splitAtLineEnd` is a method on `*ObjectConsExpr` but never uses its receiver. It is a pure token helper, and it repeats the rule that a line comment ending in '\n' ends the line, which `partitionLineEndTokens` in `parser.go` already encodes.
kept.fix: Make it a package-level function, `splitAtLineEnd(toks Tokens) (Tokens, Tokens, bool)`, and update the three call sites. Put the shared check, whether a token ends a line (`TokenNewline`, or `TokenComment` whose bytes end in '\n'), in one small helper. Use that helper from both `splitAtLineEnd` and `partitionLineEndTokens`.
kept.why: splitAtLineEnd never uses its receiver `o`. It is a pure token helper, and three call sites pass through `o.` for no reason. The rule that a token ends a line (a newline, or a comment ending in '\n') is also written again in partitionLineEndTokens. One small predicate for that rule is a reasonable shared helper.
